newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL RUBBER ENDS UP ON COVERING, CURRENCY CONCERN.
newsitem.headline: KL RUBBER ENDS UP ON COVERING, CURRENCY CONCERN.

text.p: The rubber market ended slightly higher after a fairly quiet trading day, with the currency factor and some sales to Italy helping prices, dealers said.
"The market was fairly quiet. Prices rose because of Tokyo's gains, and a weak ringgit," a dealer said. "Most buyers were still sitting at the sidelines, watching regional currency movements."
"By right, the market should have moved up in tandem with the ringgit fall yesterday. But it did not, so today there was some adjustment," the dealer said.
A government official said some small quantities of SMR 20 were traded to Italy for September shipment
Dealers saw SMR 20 being offered at 244 cents a kg, SMR CV at 289 cents, SMR L at 272, SMR 5 at 253, SMR 10 at 246 and drum latex at 189.
Dealers said Far East buyers were not too keen to deal amid uncertainty in regional currencies.
Most European factories are also closed for the summer holidays, they said.
